understanding: The task is to perform a reflective analysis and design exercise, not implementation. I must examine an external expert's analysis of memory weaknesses (tmp/memory-weakness-analysis.md) and cross-reference each of the 16 weaknesses against the actual codebase (lib/memory.ps1, tools/memory-tail.ps1, lib/librarian.ps1, code-index, context-builder, [[PROJECT_*]] markers). For each weakness, I must honestly classify its status: (a) already addressed in code, (b) partially addressed, or (c) genuinely problematic. I must not trust the analysis blindly but verify against the code. Then, I must select 2-3 high-leverage improvements that reuse existing mechanisms (typed memory, trust/status, freshness, librarian, evidence-fields) without introducing new layers or validators. I must also evaluate the 7 priorities from the analysis, especially authority-levels, auto-evidence-enrichment, lazy freshness, and memory_status heartbeat, identifying which are not yet present and which is cheapest to implement. The output is a durable plan in decisions/ with a weakness-status-verdict table and atomic improvement descriptions.
summary: I will produce a plan that systematically verifies each of the 16 weaknesses against the existing memory code, classifies them as already closed, partially closed, or genuinely painful, and selects 2-3 improvements that leverage existing typed memory, trust/status, freshness, librarian, and evidence-fields. The plan will include an evaluation of the 7 priorities, identifying gaps and the cheapest implementation path, all without adding new layers or validators.

decision_atoms.statement: Verify each of the 16 weaknesses against actual code in lib/memory.ps1, tools/memory-tail.ps1, lib/librarian.ps1, code-index, context-builder, and [[PROJECT_*]] markers.
decision_atoms.reason: The task explicitly requires not trusting the external analysis at face value; code is the source of truth. This ensures the resulting plan is grounded in reality.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Time-consuming to manually cross-reference, but prevents designing solutions for non-existent or already-solved problems.

decision_atoms.statement: Select exactly 2-3 improvements that reuse existing mechanisms (typed memory, trust/status, freshness, librarian, evidence-fields) and do not introduce new layers or validators.
decision_atoms.reason: The constraints mandate strengthening existing architecture rather than proliferating complexity, aligning with Foundation #2's principle of 'not more checks — more structure/evidence/budgets/contracts'.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Limits the scope of possible improvements, but ensures architectural coherence and avoids bloat.

decision_atoms.statement: Evaluate the 7 priorities from the analysis, specifically authority-levels, auto-evidence-enrichment, lazy freshness, and memory_status heartbeat, identifying which are absent and which is cheapest to implement.
decision_atoms.reason: The task explicitly requires this evaluation to guide the selection of high-leverage, low-cost improvements.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Focusing on these four may miss other valuable priorities, but they are explicitly called out as needing special assessment.

decision_atoms.statement: Produce a durable plan file in decisions/ with a weakness-status-verdict table and atomic improvement descriptions (file, change, acceptance, what is reused, risk).
decision_atoms.reason: The output format is specified and must be durable for operator review, ensuring traceability and accountability.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Structured output may constrain creative design, but provides clarity and auditability.

assumptions: The external analysis file tmp/memory-weakness-analysis.md exists and contains 16 weaknesses and 7 priorities as described.
The code files (lib/memory.ps1, tools/memory-tail.ps1, lib/librarian.ps1, code-index, context-builder) are accessible and reflect the current state of the memory system.
The self-reflection document decisions/dec-20260620-032229-2bd892/self_reflection_directions.md aligns with the analysis's main thesis.
Existing mechanisms (typed memory, trust/status, freshness, librarian, evidence-fields) are well-defined and can be extended without breaking changes.
The operator will review the plan for integrity, adherence to 'no new mechanisms', and atomicity of improvements.

risks.risk: The external analysis may misidentify weaknesses that are already adequately addressed in code, leading to wasted effort if not properly verified.
risks.mitigation: Rigorous cross-referencing of each weakness against actual code, with explicit evidence in the verdict column.

risks.risk: Selected improvements may inadvertently introduce hidden complexity or dependencies that violate the 'no new layers' constraint.
risks.mitigation: Each improvement will be designed to explicitly reuse existing mechanisms and will be reviewed against the constraint before finalizing the plan.

risks.risk: The plan may be too abstract or miss critical implementation details, making it non-durable or non-actionable.
risks.mitigation: Atomic descriptions with file, change, acceptance criteria, and risk will ensure concreteness and testability.

minimal_version: Plan with weakness-status-verdict table covering all 16 weaknesses, classification of each as a/b/c, and 2 improvements that reuse existing mechanisms, with evaluation of the 4 specified priorities.
advanced_version: Plan with detailed code references for each weakness classification, 3 improvements with full atomic descriptions, comprehensive evaluation of all 7 priorities with cost-benefit analysis, and a traceability matrix linking improvements to specific weaknesses and existing mechanisms.
